newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-WAIKATO START SUPER 12 WITH TENSE WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WAIKATO START SUPER 12 WITH TENSE WIN.

text.p: All Black winger Glen Osborne launched the new Super 12 season with a try 12 minutes from time to secure a tense 23-18 win for the Waikato Chiefs over the Wellington Hurricanes on Friday.

The teams were level at 18-18 before veteran centre Frank Bunce flicked a high pass over two defenders to his team-mate, who dived over to give the Chiefs a 23-18 win in front of a capacity 18,000 crowd.

The Hurricanes made a storming start to the match, full-back Jarrod Cunningham scoring in the right corner just a minute into the game, but Waikato led 11-8 at half-time thanks to a 22nd minute try by Walter Little and two penalties from Matthew Cooper.
Jon Preston levelled the scores with an early second-half penalty and Tana Umaga then raced 30 metres for a try to put the Hurricanes back in front.
But a superb run by Cooper on the blindside was rewarded with a try by Eric Rush and Cooper's conversion set the stage for Bunce and Osborne to settle the issue.
The bad news for Waikato was an injury to Little who failed to reappear in the second half.
He appeared to be hit by a knee in the head when he dived over for his try and if he has suffered concussion, as feared by Chiefs officials, he will be out for a mandatory three weeks.
Little extends a long list of All Black injuries which include Zinzan Brooke, Christian Cullen, Michael Jones, Josh Kronfeld, Andrew Blowers, Charles Reichelmann and Craig Dowd.

Waikato Chiefs - Matthew Cooper, Eric Rush, Frank Bunce, Walter Little, Glen Osborne; Ian Foster, Mark Robinson; Deon Muir, Dean Anglesey, Glenn Taylor, Ian Jones (captain, Errol Brain, Richard Loe, Greg Smith, Michael Collins.

Wellington Hurricanes - Jarrod Cunningham; Tana Umaga, Alama Ieremia, Roger Randle, Jason O'Halloran; Stephen Bachop, Jon Preston; Karl Williams, Filo Tiatia, Mike Russell, Mark Cooksley, Chresten Davis, Phil Coffin, Norm Hewitt, Mark Allen (captain).
